A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BindWeave research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison. The original appendix examples remain identifiable after renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original OpenS2V-Eval results, a quantitative conditioning ablation in Table 2, and generated-video comparisons in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a user study, training diagnostics and qualitative stress tests.

M1.justification: The proposed MLLM–MLP–T5–DiT architecture, CLIP/VAE conditioning, objectives and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 describes unsuccessful pilot alternatives without changing the final method.

E1.justification: Training data and OpenS2V-Eval coverage are retained. Section 4.6 adds deliberate reference–prompt conflicts involving expressions, clothing and poses, while Appendix A.4 adds five-reference composition cases. These extend test conditions within the existing subject-to-video task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all external comparators. Appendix A.3 newly reports an evaluated MLLM+Q-Former+DiT alternative. The added user study compares six existing baseline families: SkyReels, Vidu, MAGREF, Phantom, Kling and VACE.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 introduces a distinct human-evaluation protocol: 20 participants, anonymized and randomly assigned samples, and 1–5 ratings for subject consistency, prompt following, motion quality and video quality. The existing 180-video benchmark protocol and training/inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence with targeted copy-paste tests, additional complex multi-reference T5-only comparisons, and pilot-architecture analysis. Figure 9 adds loss and gradient-norm traces for the previously reported unstable MLLM-only configuration; Appendix A.3 also reports unsuccessful Q-Former conditioning.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new user study supplies mean opinion scores without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain every numerical result. New Table 3 reports BindWeave's overall human score of 3.76 versus VACE's 3.73, and subject-consistency scores of 3.94 versus 3.88. Training traces and new qualitative comparisons substantially expand reported outcomes without establishing improved performance on the unchanged benchmark.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 and their mathematical content are unchanged. The new appendix material supplies empirical observations and architectural explanations, not new definitions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning cross-modal integration, subject consistency and superior OpenS2V performance. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new expression, clothing and pose tests as evidence against pixel copying. Appendices A.3–A.4 expand explanations of MLLM-only training instability and the encoders' complementary roles in compositional reasoning, building on interpretations already present in v1.

D1.justification: The documented connector implementation, training budget, hardware description, hyperparameters, augmentations and inference settings remain unchanged. The project link and promised code/model release are also unchanged; the pilot descriptions add no detailed implementation settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wu et al. (2025), 'Video repurposing from user generated content: A large-scale dataset and benchmark,' to the introduction and references. The related-work discussion and positioning against shallow multimodal fusion otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects wording and the 'BinWeave' typo, regularizes citations, and adds conference headers, an affiliation and acknowledgments. New experiment and appendix subsections extend the existing structure without substantially rewriting the established narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3 and four figures: a user-study radar chart, conflict-scenario examples, training diagnostics and complex multi-reference comparisons. Existing figures are retained; v1 Figures 7–10 become v2 Figures 11–14, with appendix explanations redistributed around them.

improvement.justification: The user study and targeted diagnostic figures provide useful additional support for perceptual quality, conditioning choices and resistance to copy-paste artifacts. The improvement is limited: existing benchmark results are unchanged, the human-score advantage is small and lacks uncertainty estimates, and the additional architectural evidence remains largely qualitative.
